environment.tool: manual review of release/000002 + live compiled binary against a kv config with two doc roots

findings.description: localfile picks root = host==bhost ? broot : root, then replaces root with aliasroot when the decoded path begins with the alias prefix. Host validation has already completed, so nothing re-checks that the alias root belongs to the winning vhost. With host_root beta and alias set, GET /alias/hello.txt under Host: beta.test returns the alias file while /ten.txt on the same vhost is 404. Read-scope bypass; RCE-adjacent if the alias root holds an executable the upstream would run.
findings.title: The alias branch overwrites the vhost-selected document root after host validation, so a confined vhost reads the alias root

findings.description: GET /alias%2fhello.txt returns the same file because %2f decodes to the separator that satisfies the prefix compare. The encoded spelling defeats a raw-prefix check placed in front of the proxy.
findings.title: The alias prefix is matched on the decoded path, so %2f spelling reaches the same alias root and bypasses nothing extra but hides the path from the vhost

limitations: Read-scope only on this build (no executor in the alias root)
methods: Marked distinct content in alpha, beta and alias roots
Confirmed beta confinement with an alpha-only file
Drove alias plain and %2f forms from the beta vhost
